mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stop improving and remain deeply negative, weekday footfall into retail corridors stays suppressed and RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES stayed below -25 and TRANSIT below -27 across all four weeks
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC averages above its last-28-day mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain at or below their current weak levels for the full next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS from a weak week to a positive week diverts discretionary outings away from shopping trips; when PARKS rises above its recent mean, RETAIL_REC falls within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 10 points week-on-week after a negative week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from 15.7 to 2.0 after -4.7 in the prior week
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not weaken within 14 days after a week in which PARKS jumps above 10 and stays elevated relative to the prior week.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve together, commute-linked shopping and incidental purchases expand, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved from t-2w to t-0w despite remaining negative
failure_condition: Reject if simultaneous four-week improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES is followed by no increase, or a decrease, in RETAIL_REC relative to the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline while WORKPLACES remain far below baseline, people shift toward home-centered routines and neighborhood buying, keeping RETAIL_REC below the previous four-week average over the next month.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -20 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +3
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is positive in all four weeks while WORKPLACES is strongly negative
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean while WORKPLACES stays below -20 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +3 through the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A short-lived PARKS spike followed by a drop signals weather-driven outdoor substitution rather than durable demand, and retail mobility then reverts downward within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS swings by at least 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS changed from 8.3 to -4.7 to 15.7 to 2.0 across the snapshot
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC fails to decline within 7 days after a PARKS swing of 10 points or more.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM remains only mildly negative while RETAIL_REC is more negative, households are substituting essentials for discretionary shopping, and retail mobility stays depressed over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed near -5 while RETAIL_REC stayed near -25
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises for two consecutive weeks without a matching deterioration in GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent recovery in TRANSIT and PARKS increases city-center trip chaining: people combine outdoor leisure with shopping, which lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 5 points and PARKS stays positive for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -34.1 to -27.9 and PARKS was positive in two of four weeks
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior four-week mean after TRANSIT improves by at least 5 points and PARKS remains positive for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, a fall in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES below their recent levels directly suppresses nonessential shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -30 and WORKPLACES falls below -30 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both series were near or below -30 in multiple weeks
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both drop below -30 in the same week.
